title: Sprachgebrauch und Sprachidentitäten
summary: How does language shape our identity? How do we construct different identities through language? What norms govern our use of language – and how do these change over time, depending on the people involved? What do historical sources reveal about the writers of the time and their writing practices? This anthology explores these and other questions concerning the role of language in processes of social and technological change. It comprises German- and English-language contributions that offer interesting insights into the variability of individual languages and are divided into three parts: Language use and linguistic identities in historical written records (Part I), language use at the intersection of norm, variation and didactics (Part II), and language use, linguistic identities and indexicality in transition (Part III). In addition, the introduction explains the concept of linguistic identity underpinning the anthology and the arguments in favour of assuming the existence of multiple linguistic identities.
